items.rootCause: RemoteGameHost.comeBack() stopped retrying at the seat's deadline: the phone noticing the loss + soft 10 s + grace 15 s + server notice 4.5 s + 1 s, about 30.5 s. The server keeps a finished game's room for closeAfterGameMs (60 s) and hands the finished game, with its result, to a player who comes back by code (spec 16.2, 'after the end of the game'). The app never used that window. So a phone whose network came back after ~30 s could not learn that it lost by abandonment. It ended on the generic 'lost' error ('החיבור לשרת המשחק אבד ולא הצלחנו לחזור אליו.'). The reported ~2 minutes after Wi-Fi came back is NOT explained by the code. Each try is capped at 5 s and the loop has a hard deadline, so the loop cannot run that long. Possible causes: the phone noticed the loss late, or Android's HTTP stack hung on a dead pooled connection after the network changed, so every try timed out as 'network'. The final screen (failure 'lost', code 'network') fits the loop ending on a try that timed out.
items.fix: apps/mobile/src/net/remoteGameHost.ts: new option afterGraceRetryMs (default 60_000). Past the seat's deadline, in a game that was running, the host keeps trying for that long: the token first, then a rejoin by code. A network that comes back late now brings the finished game (the abandonment result) within a try or two. A room already gone answers notFound/roomGone, and the host stops at once. When it gives up after graceEndsAt, OnlineInfo gets pastGrace: true. connectionStatus.ts maps that to a new ConnectionFailure 'expired'. ConnectionError shows title 'לא חזרת למשחק בזמן' and body 'החיבור לא חזר בזמן, ולכן המשחק נחשב נטישה.' (new keys connection.error.expiredTitle and connection.error.body.expired, in all 19 locales). SelfReconnecting's timer at 0 seconds now shows 'הזמן נגמר · בודקים מול השרת…' (existing strings) instead of 'יש לך עוד 0 שניות לחזור', while the host keeps trying in the extra window.

issues.problem: The fix does not explain the reported ~2 minutes on 'ללא חיבור', and the most likely device explanation is still not covered. In an ~80 s airplane test the screen probably timed out. Samsung's default timeout is 30 s, and the QA reset does not set stay-awake. With the screen off, AppState goes to 'background' and isStale() halts comeBack(). The old UI frame ('ללא חיבור', the self card's soft 'unstable' label) then stays until the phone is woken. On wake, comeBack() makes exactly one try even when the time is already past giveUpAt (the deadline check runs only after a failed try). Wi-Fi is often still reassociating right after wake or after airplane mode goes off, so that one try fails as 'network' and the host closes at once. That matches the screenshot (code 'network', generic 'lost'). With the new code, a wake more than about 90 s after the loss still gets one try and then the 'expired' screen. The Hebrew message is clear, but the result is never fetched, even when the room is still alive.
issues.evidence: remoteGameHost.ts onAppState(): 'background' while status is 'reconnecting' → backgrounded=true, run++ (the loop goes stale). 'active' → comeBack(). In comeBack(), the check `if (!this.lost || this.now() >= this.giveUpAt(this.lost)) break;` comes after `await this.tryOnce(run)`, so a single try is made past the deadline. fixcheck-apk16.json: P3 airplane ~80 s, no logcat, and the stay-awake state is not recorded. Screenshot fix11-RF8Y30L038L-after-airplane.png shows chip 'network' (a timed-out or failed fetch) and no notFound. The fixer could not explain the 2 min from the code either and marked the item 'partial'.
issues.suggestion: After a return to the foreground (or after any first try past the deadline), allow a small minimum retry window, e.g. at least ~8–10 s or 3 tries, before closing, so a network that is still coming up can bring the finished game. In the device check, keep the screen on (adb shell svc power stayon true, or touch the screen) and capture logcat '[online]' lines, including 'in the background: disconnecting' and 'back in the foreground: reconnecting'. That confirms or rules out the background freeze as the cause of the 2 minutes.

items.rootCause: There were two causes. (1) RemoteGameHost.comeBack() stopped at the seat's deadline: the phone noticing the loss, plus soft 10 s, grace 15 s, server notice 4.5 s and 1 s, about 30.5 s. The server keeps a finished game's room for closeAfterGameMs (60 s) and gives that finished game, with its result, to a player who comes back by code (spec 16.2). The app never used that window, so a network that came back after about 30 s ended on the generic 'lost' error. (2) Raised in review, and the most likely reason for the ~2 minutes. In an ~80 s airplane test the screen times out (Samsung default 30 s; the QA reset does not set stay-awake). AppState goes to 'background', and the loop is frozen on purpose (isStale) until the phone is woken, so the old 'ללא חיבור' frame stays until then. On wake, comeBack() made exactly ONE try past giveUpAt, because the deadline is checked only after a failed try. Right after a wake or after airplane mode goes off, Wi-Fi is often still joining, so that one try timed out as 'network'. The host then closed at once. That matches the screenshot exactly: generic 'lost', code 'network', no notFound. The code alone can't prove (2); a logcat with the '[online]' lines would confirm it.
items.fix: apps/mobile/src/net/remoteGameHost.ts. (a) From round 1: option afterGraceRetryMs (60 s). Past the seat's deadline, in a game that was running, the host keeps trying (the token, then a rejoin by code), so a late network still brings the finished game with the abandonment result. A room that is already gone (notFound/roomGone) stops the host at once. Giving up after graceEndsAt sets OnlineInfo.pastGrace. The loop gives up only at max(giveUpAt, tryUntil), so a wake long past every deadline gets several tries (250 ms / 500 ms / 1 s backoff) over 10 s, not one. A network still coming up can then fetch the finished game, or the gone room answers notFound and the 'expired' screen follows. items.rootCause: There were two causes. (1) RemoteGameHost.comeBack() stopped at the seat's deadline: the phone noticing the loss, plus soft 10 s, grace 15 s, server notice 4.5 s and 1 s, about 30.5 s. The server keeps a finished game's room for closeAfterGameMs (60 s) and gives that finished game, with its result, to a player who comes back by code (spec 16.2). The app never used that window, so a network that came back after about 30 s ended on the generic 'lost' error. (2) Raised in review, and the most likely reason for the ~2 minutes. In an ~80 s airplane test the screen times out (Samsung default 30 s; the QA reset does not set stay-awake). On wake, comeBack() made exactly ONE try past giveUpAt, because the deadline is checked only after a failed try. Right after a wake or after airplane mode goes off, Wi-Fi is often still joining, so that one try timed out as 'network'. The host then closed at once. items.rootCause: What the loop-12 measurements show: on Android, react-native-screens' 'fade' is two 150 ms view animations (rns_fade_in.xml and rns_fade_out.xml). They run on a timer on the UI thread. On the same thread, at the same moment, the results screen mounts and draws for the first time. The push commit used to mount the whole results screen: the hero, then the opponents or ranking with their SVG avatars, the rating, the best move, the stats, the awards, the action bar and the confetti, plus their Reanimated 'entering' setups. Frame stats show frames of 60–150 ms: anim (Fabric mount and Reanimated) 52–60 ms, draw 36–52 ms, vsync-late 66–78 ms. So the 150 ms fade got only 0–2 frames. In 3 of 5 runs without Reduced Motion the board went in one frame and the results came in only partly drawn (2 hard cuts, 1 fade stuck at about 50% for 91 ms). Every cut had a 305–857 ms gap from mount to transition; the smooth runs had 168–269 ms. Draw that frame with the incoming screen near 0 and you get the reported 'only the background' frame. Ruled out on the device (11 runs): activity recreation or a root swap (no relaunch or config-change lines), an ambient SurfaceView cycle (no surfaceCreated or surfaceDestroyed, and the digits show in every cut frame), and Modals or windows (no window add or remove). Not explained by this evidence: the original f71 (Reduced Motion on) had no ambient digits at all, but every cut frame measured has digits. Also, 0 of 6 Reduced Motion runs cut. So f71 itself was not reproduced, and its exact cause is not proven. The fade timing is native (Android ignores animationDuration, and the XML tweens are inside react-native-screens), so the fix has to be on the JS side.

rep.notes: I marked the item partial on purpose. The measurements support one mechanism: Android's fixed 150 ms fade, which runs on a timer on the UI thread, overlaps the results' heavy first mount and draw. That causes the one-frame cuts and the stalled fades. I removed the part the app controls: the push commit now holds only the top bar, the hero and the score on Android, and the rest mounts after the opening transitionEnd (fallback 1000 ms). The reported f71 frame (Reduced Motion on, no ambient digits) was not reproduced in 6 Reduced Motion runs, and its missing digits do not match any measured cut frame (all of them show the digits). If it comes back after this APK, the next lead is window or SurfaceView compositing, not navigation. Facts for that: AmbientStill under Reduced Motion is an opaque SurfaceView, so it shows through a hole in the window, and a window frame drawn without that hole would show only the root background #0f1218. Things I did not change: react-native-screens' native durations (Android ignores animationDuration), the transition type in theme/transitions.ts (both fade_from_bottom and none would change motion.md), and ResultsVersus (other agents). Small timing drift: the rating count and the avatars' end reactions in ResultsVersus now start when their section mounts, so up to the transition length later (about 150–300 ms). issues.problem: The 1000 ms fallback can end the wait in the middle of the fade, in exactly the slow case the measurements recorded. If that happens, the rest of the screen mounts during the fade and brings back the overlap the fix is meant to remove. The hook ends the wait on whichever comes first: transitionEnd or the 1000 ms timer. The timer starts when the JS effect runs, which is before the UI thread mounts the screen.
issues.evidence: useStackEntered.ts: `RESULTS_REST_FALLBACK_MS = 1000` and `setTimeout(done, from + fallbackMs - Date.now())`. The device data has rmoff4 with the transition starting +857 ms after the mount (initGoToTop). The Android fade is a fixed 150 ms (transitions.ts ANDROID_FADE_MS), so it ends at about +1007 ms, and later if frames stall. In that run the fallback fires at about 1000 ms from the JS commit, which is inside the fade. The ranking or opponents with SVG avatars, the rating, the stats, the action bar and their Reanimated entering setups then mount and draw during the transition, which is the mechanism the fix targets. The fix assumes that a lighter push commit shortens the 305–857 ms gap. No measurement backs that yet.
issues.suggestion: Do not let the timer end the wait while a transition is known to be running. Also listen for the route's 'transitionStart' (closing false; native-stack emits it from onWillAppear). items.rootCause:
The loop-12 measurements point to two causes. Neither is the sound, which the evidence rules out: with sound off the split and the stall are the same size.

(1) The hit clock was read from the server. The hit clock starts at elapsedOf(hit, clock.now()), and on the receiver that clock is server-synced (RemoteGameHost.clock = phone time + offset). By the time the receiver commits the hit, the server already counts it as about 100–200 ms in: the time from the sender's tap, through the server, to this phone. The frame that mounts the hit then took 150–230 ms by framestats, and the clock kept running through it. So the first frame anyone saw was already past the 240 ms fade-in. Each part (the RN dim, the RN banner, the Skia overlay) popped in at full strength in a single frame, at whatever moment it happened to reach the screen. This matches 'full strength in one frame' in every run. It also matches the second warp: lower latency left part of the fade, so the dim faded in over 2 steps.

(2) A new Skia surface at every warp. HitLayer returned null between hits, so each warp mounted a new WarpOverlay <Canvas>. In RN Skia 2.6.2 on Android that is a new non-opaque SkiaTextureView (SkiaBaseView → SkiaTextureView). Its picture shows only after several steps: onSurfaceTextureAvailable on the next draw, then OpenGLContext::MakeWindow, then a requestRedraw, a Skia draw and a present, and then HWUI latching the texture on a later frame. That is why the overlay was always last, 94–348 ms after TSA, while the banner and the dim are plain views that show in the mount commit itself. The 'updateAndRelease() failed' lines are RNSkOpenGLCanvasProvider calling SurfaceTexture.updateTexImage from a context the texture is not attached to. They are harmless and not the cause.

This also explains why HitRehearsal did not help: it makes and then drops its own canvases.

What it rules out:
- the sound;
- GC;
- the four separate clocks of earlier loops (already one clock).

Not fixed here: the remaining cost of the effect itself while it runs (15–48 ms UI anim and 12–36 ms RenderThread per frame). That is native and Reanimated/Skia work, outside this item.
items.fix:
Both fixes are JS-side mitigations for a native surface lifecycle that JS cannot change.

(1) The hit clock starts from the first frame on this phone (components/interference/hitClock.ts).
- A hit that reaches the phone at most HIT_LATE_START_MS = 500 ms into its time starts at 0. A later one (app back mid-hit) starts where it is. A hit that arrives frozen also starts where it stands.
- A new worklet, hitClockStep, moves the clock at the pace that lands it on totalMs exactly at endsAt. It catches up a few % faster than real time, so the hit still ends exactly at the end (spec §7.2).
- While the hit comes in (first 480 ms: the fade-in plus the tilt's ease-in), one frame counts for at most HIT_MAX_START_STEP_MS = 34 ms. A 150–230 ms mount frame can no longer jump the fade to full strength.
- The first frame callback only anchors the clock.
- When the deadline moves while a hit is on (a freeze), the clock goes on from where it is drawn instead of jumping back.
- The dim, the overlay, the banner (bannerEnter) and the tilt all read this one shared clock. They fade in together from 0, and the tilt still waits for the fade-in.

(2) The warp canvas is mounted ahead (screens/game/hit/HitLayer.tsx).
- New prop standby?: InterferenceKind. Between hits, HitLayer keeps that kind's effect mounted in its region at opacity 0, drawn at elapsed 0, which is transparent. It has no banner and nothing for screen readers, and it is pointerEvents none.
- So the TextureView, its surface and its first texture all exist before the warp. The hit only switches the region's opacity and moves the shared clock.
- The effect is wrapped in React.memo, so it does not re-render on every countdown tick.
- The idle testIDs are 'hit-layer-standby' and 'hit-layer-standby-region', so existing 'hit-layer-region gone at the end' checks still hold.
- GameScreen passes standby='warp' only when view.rules.interferences is on and the game's interferenceKinds include 'warp'. A practice (D44) mounts nothing.

Reduced Motion: unchanged. The same still cover and the 200 ms fade come from the same clock, and the standby uses the same `reduce`.

items.rootCause:
The device evidence points to three separate things.

(1) Sound-off excess (+1.0-1.3 s, confirmed from the code). GameScreen.tsx mounted with `useEffect(() => { preloadCues(); }, [])` and never checked the sound setting. sfx.preload() does not check it either: only play() does. The lobby warm-up (warmGame.ts soundStep) and useWarmHitCues both skip players when sound is off. So a cold joiner with sound off reached /game with no players made, and the game screen built all 13 under GO!. expo-audio builds each one on the UI thread while JS waits, which matches the >=1.29 s with no app frame and the ~20 AudioTrack setVolume burst just before the mount (3 of 3 sound-off runs, none with sound on). All of that was for players that never play.

(2) The blank frame between the lobby and '3' (12 of 12 count starts, confirmed from the code). FriendsCountdown wrapped its whole column (avatars, step, 'התכוננו…') in an Animated.View with useEnter(), so it mounts at opacity 0 and fades in over 200 ms. Its first frame therefore showed the header only. On the host the column visibly fades in from 0 after 1-2 empty frames. On the joiner the next frame is already full: its fade most likely finished during the 70-101 ms stall while the count mounted. motion.md (friends.countdown) only asks the step to slam or fade, not the players.

(3) The baseline GO→mount of ~0.6 s past the 250 ms hold, on both phones. The friends route calls router.replace('/game') friendsGoHoldMs (250 ms on Android) after GO! is drawn. It waits longer only if the game state arrives later. The 'mount' anchor (StatusBar) fires after the game route's first JS commit, so the extra ~0.6 s is the game screen's own JS render and commit, plus however late the game state arrives. Ranked shows the same 1.0-1.1 s through MatchScreen and GoCover. It is not sound (the sound-on host builds no players) and not navigation (no window events). The current logs cannot tell the state's arrival from the render, so I did not change it.

(4) The startInputInner calls per step are not tied to anything here. /friends/join is replaced, not left under the room, so the measurements do not explain them. Not changed.
